label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L=3-4)
explanation: Fires almost only at the <DEL> step (99.8% of activations, 99.96% of mass), so it is a delimiter detector. It is strongly gated by sequence length: active on about 96% of <DEL> steps when L=3, about 43% when L=4, about 11% when L=5, under 2% for L=6-8, with a small rise again at L=9. Mean magnitude is highest at L=3 (L=3 holds 40% of mass from 19% of activations). Within L=4-5, whether it fires depends on the content in a diffuse way: some first tokens (c, 2, o) give 2.5-2.8x lift, and having fewer digits in the sequence helps, but no simple token rule improved F1. It never fires during the copy phase and essentially never during the original tokens (23 of 646k steps). The predicate catches 80% of mass on dev, but precision is about 0.5 because many L=4 <DEL> steps stay silent.
